name: Bevacizumab
route_note: IV infusion every 2–3 weeks in oncology; intravitreal injection for neovascular AMD (widely off-label; Lytenava licensed in the EU)

discovery.note: Humanised form of the murine anti-VEGF antibody A.4.6.1; VEGF itself was cloned at Genentech by Napoleone Ferrara in 1989.

tagline: First angiogenesis inhibitor approved for cancer, blocking VEGF-A
summary: Bevacizumab is a humanised monoclonal antibody that neutralises vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGF-A). It was the first anti-angiogenic drug approved for cancer and is used with chemotherapy in colorectal, lung, ovarian, cervical and other cancers; it is also widely used off-label by intravitreal injection for retinal disease.
mechanism: Bevacizumab binds all isoforms of VEGF-A and prevents it from activating VEGF receptors (VEGFR-1 and VEGFR-2) on endothelial cells.

Blocking VEGF signalling inhibits new blood-vessel formation, causes regression of immature tumour vessels and normalises the remaining vasculature, which may improve chemotherapy delivery. In the eye it reduces leakage and growth of abnormal choroidal vessels.
uses: Ovarian, fallopian tube and primary peritoneal cancer

history.title: VEGF cloned
history.detail: Napoleone Ferrara and colleagues at Genentech isolate and clone VEGF.

history.title: AVF2107g trial
history.detail: Adding bevacizumab to IFL chemotherapy prolongs survival in metastatic colorectal cancer.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved as Avastin for first-line metastatic colorectal cancer.

history.title: Lung cancer
history.detail: Approved for non-squamous NSCLC with carboplatin–paclitaxel.

history.title: Breast indication revoked
history.detail: FDA revokes the accelerated approval for metastatic breast cancer after confirmatory trials fail to show sufficient benefit.

history.title: First biosimilar
history.detail: FDA approves Mvasi (bevacizumab-awwb), the first US biosimilar for cancer treatment.

history.title: Liver cancer
history.detail: Approved with atezolizumab for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (IMbrave150).

history.title: Ophthalmic licence
history.detail: The EU approves Lytenava (bevacizumab gamma) for neovascular age-related macular degeneration.

pk.metabolism: Proteolytic catabolism to peptides and amino acids (no CYP metabolism)
pk.excretion: Not renally excreted as intact antibody; cleared by catabolism and target-mediated uptake

facts: Inexpensive repackaged intravitreal bevacizumab is used worldwide off-label for wet AMD; the CATT trial found it comparable to ranibizumab.
It is usually withheld for several weeks before and after elective surgery because it impairs wound healing.
